mechanics.name: Road Life
mechanics.currentEffect: While injured and repairing a Generator, hitting a basic Great Skill Check gives 1 Token and missing a basic Skill Check removes 1 Token. At 6/5/4 Tokens, you can heal yourself; spending all Tokens lets you self-heal 10% faster. After you stop healing, this self-heal effect ends after 4 seconds.
activation: Be Injured and repairing a Generator to gain or lose Tokens from basic Repair Skill Checks.
Reach 6/5/4 Tokens to gain the ability to self-heal.
Begin self-healing to spend all Tokens and receive the 10% self-heal speed bonus.
Ends/deactivates when: Stopping the self-heal starts a 4-second grace period; after 4 seconds the granted self-heal effect ends.
Ends/deactivates when: Missed basic Repair Skill Checks remove 1 Token while the token-building condition is active.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (10.2.0): Reworked into a Repair-Skill-Check token system that grants self-healing at 6/5/4 Tokens, spends all Tokens on use, gives 10% faster self-healing, and ends 4 seconds after healing stops.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: While injured on Generators, Great checks build and missed checks remove tokens; reaching the tier threshold lets you spend them to self-heal slightly faster.
duration: Granted self-heal ability persists for 4 seconds after stopping the heal before ending.
mechanics.tokenOrStackBehavior: While Injured and repairing, basic Great Skill Checks add 1 Token and missed basic Skill Checks remove 1. Threshold is 6/5/4 by tier. Starting the granted self-heal spends all Tokens.
specialInteractions: The final live self-heal speed bonus is 10%, not the higher PTB test value.

editorial.summary: While injured on a Generator, earn Tokens from Great basic Skill Checks; at the threshold, spend them to self-heal 10% faster.
useCases: Convert productive injured Generator repair into access to a repeatable self-heal.
Stay productive while charging the perk instead of spending time on a separate setup objective.
Use it when independent self-reset access is more valuable than carrying a dedicated healing perk or item.
counters: Token acquisition depends on Great basic Skill Check frequency and execution, so charge time varies substantially.
Missed checks cost progress, and the practical effect of interruptions still needs controlled testing.
Stake Out is not a partner: its special Skill Checks replace the basic checks Road Life needs while Tokens are held.
pros: The completed self-heal is fast enough to be meaningful.
The perk charges during productive Generator work.
Live gameplay supports repeatable use rather than a one-use payoff.
cons: The Token economy is still unmeasured and is the main reason the exact rank is provisional.
Requires staying injured while repairing to build toward the heal.
analysis: Road Life is best understood as a self-heal access perk whose reward is strong once earned. Live gameplay showed the completed heal is practically useful and can be earned again, so the old one-use and 100%-speed framing is obsolete.
The unresolved variable is the Token economy. The precision review could not justify the optimistic charge-rate assumption behind rank #58, so the perk moved to #65 with a wide credible range.

A neutral working assumption is roughly one activation per generator's worth of injured repair for a player who hits most Great checks. That is an assumption to test, not a mechanic to encode as fact.
Because setup happens during productive repair, Road Life still compares favorably with slower or travel-dependent self-heal options even when its charge time is imperfect.
editorial.verdict: A genuinely useful self-heal once charged, held to a provisional mid-B rank because the real Token-acquisition rate is still the unanswered question.
